articles.title: White Ribbon Football Tournament returns to Rochdale for 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced the return of its annual White Ribbon Football Tournament, bringing together teams from across the authority to promote the campaign to end violence against women and girls.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that its annual White Ribbon Football Tournament will return on Tuesday 4 August 2026, bringing together teams from across the council in support of the White Ribbon campaign.

Before kick-off, participating teams will take the White Ribbon pledge, reaffirming their commitment to helping end violence against women and girls.

The council is a White Ribbon accredited organisation and says the tournament has been organised entirely by members of staff in their own time to raise awareness of the campaign and encourage conversations around preventing abuse and violence.

Residents are encouraged to attend and cheer on the teams throughout the day. While places in the tournament itself are limited, spectators are welcome.

The tournament takes place at Heywood Sports Village on Tuesday 4 August 2026, and spectators are welcome.

The White Ribbon campaign works to engage men and boys in preventing violence against women and girls by promoting positive attitudes, respectful relationships and challenging harmful behaviours.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Thanks Volunteers for Successful Improvement Week
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has thanked volunteers and supporters for their contributions during the recent Volunteers Week, which saw significant improvements made to the Crown Oil Arena.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has expressed gratitude to everyone who supported its 2026 Volunteers Week, which aimed to enhance the Crown Oil Arena ahead of the new season. Over five days, supporters, local businesses, community organisations, schools, and volunteers collaborated with staff from both Rochdale AFC and Rochdale AFC Community Trust to complete various improvement projects across the stadium.

During the week, volunteers contributed an impressive 351 hours of work, equivalent to approximately 2.5 months of a full-time maintenance worker's efforts. This collective time and effort have made a lasting impact on the stadium, showcasing the strength of community collaboration.

The extensive programme of work included numerous projects that have transformed the area around the Crown Oil Arena, ensuring it is in excellent condition as the club prepares to welcome supporters back for the 2026/27 campaign. The success of the week was attributed to the commitment and enthusiasm of all volunteers, whether they participated for a few hours or throughout the entire week.

Rochdale AFC also thanked those who supported the volunteers, including individuals who provided refreshments during the warm weather. Special recognition was given to Ian Watson for visiting and showing appreciation to the volunteers, as well as to partner organisations that contributed to the week's success.
